exposure: Mother's residence (Capital Area vs. outside Capital Area)
cohort: 40,982 live singleton births and 145 stillbirths (≥22 weeks or ≥500 g) in Iceland from 2000 to 2009
finding: Infants born to mothers residing outside the Capital Area in Iceland had a higher rate of cesarean delivery but a lower prevalence of gestational diabetes, hypertension, and congenital malformations, with no significant differences in birthweight, gestational age, preterm birth, or low birthweight.
mod_finding: Infants born outside the Capital Area were more likely to have been delivered by cesarean section (adjusted odds ratio 1.28; 95% CI 1.21-1.36).
birth_weight: Mean birthweight did not differ between the Capital Area and non-Capital Area.
